card: This pull request adds stream insertion operator<< overloads for commonly tested Bitcoin Core types in src/test/util/common.{h,cpp} and updates assertions across 15 unit test suites from BOOST_CHECK to BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL or BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL_COLLECTIONS. Previously, equality assertions on these types only printed a boolean failure upon mismatch, forcing developers to write temporary debugging code to inspect actual values. These string formatters also prepare the test suite for the proposed migration away from Boost unit test runner in PR 35713.
changed_since_previous: The scope and implementation remain the same; changes are minor rebasing and test macro adjustments.
evidence: PR description: 'If the `<<` operator exists, boost can use this as a debug output when a check fails (besides `BOOST_CHECK`).'
PR description notes that 'All of these display strings would be used as part of #35713, but we can also use them with boost today.'
problem: When unit test assertions using `BOOST_CHECK(a == b)` fail, Boost only reports a boolean failure without printing mismatched values. Types like `FeeFrac`, `CScript`, `CAddress`, and `CTxDestination` lacked streaming operators in the test suite, making test failures harder to debug.

risk.why: Touches only test utility helpers and unit test assertions, with no impact on production node behavior or release binaries.

scope_notes: Mostly mechanical changes across unit tests replacing `BOOST_CHECK` comparisons with `BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL` alongside new stream operators in `src/test/util/common.{h,cpp}`.
summary: Adds stream output `operator<<` overloads for common Bitcoin Core types in `src/test/util/common.{h,cpp}` so test runners can print their contents. Converts equality assertions across 15 unit test suites from bare `BOOST_CHECK(a == b)` to `BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL` or `BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL_COLLECTIONS`. This produces informative mismatch output on test failure without changing production code.
